downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.detail: PR #15009 moved the accelerometer hardware list and added LSM6DSK320X, ICM42622P and ICM42686P to it. 2025.12.5's list doesn't include these chips.
downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.note: 2025.12.5 can't select your accelerometer by name, so the setting now uses AUTO, which lets the firmware detect the sensor. After flashing, check that the accelerometer is detected and works before you fly.

downgrade:altitude-controller-gains-retu.detail: PRs #14922, #15299 and #15303 restructured the altitude hold PID and its scaling, including a feedforward scaling fix, and raised the defaults from 15 to 30. Because of this, a value from one version can't be reliably converted to the other.
downgrade:altitude-controller-gains-retu.note: Your altitude hold gains were tuned for the reworked altitude controller in 2026.6.1, so the same numbers won't behave the same way in 2025.12.5. The 2025.12.5 defaults are used instead. If you use altitude hold, re-enter values you tuned before on 2025.12.5, or test carefully from the defaults and re-tune.

downgrade:altitude-filter-range-clamped-.detail: PR #15299 raised the maximum of these altitude filter settings from 1000 to 5000 without changing the units. Older firmware still caps them at 1000.
downgrade:altitude-filter-range-clamped-.note: 2025.12.5 only accepts altitude filter values from 10 to 1000, so any value above 1000 was lowered to 1000. Values of 1000 or below carry over unchanged.

downgrade:altitude-source-rangefinder-re.detail: PR #14922 added RANGEFINDER_PREFER and RANGEFINDER_ONLY along with optical flow and rangefinder altitude hold support. 2025.12.5 only has DEFAULT, BARO_ONLY and GPS_ONLY.
downgrade:altitude-source-rangefinder-re.note: 2025.12.5 can't use the rangefinder as an altitude source, so the setting is back to DEFAULT. If you want a specific source, the choices are `set altitude_source = BARO_ONLY` or `set altitude_source = GPS_ONLY`. Check how altitude hold behaves before relying on it.

downgrade:ap-hover-throttle-low-value-re.detail: PR #14922 widened the range from 1100-1700 to 0-1700 and made 0 mean "capture hover throttle from the stick when altitude hold is engaged". Older firmware has no such mode and rejects values below 1100.
downgrade:ap-hover-throttle-low-value-re.note: 2025.12.5 can't capture hover throttle from the stick, and it only accepts values from 1100 to 1700, so your hover throttle now uses the board's default. If you use altitude or position hold, set your hover throttle again, e.g. `set ap_hover_throttle = 1275`, adjusted to where your quad actually hovers.

downgrade:ap-position-cutoff-unit-and-fi.detail: In 2025.12.5 the cutoff is 0.01 Hz per step and drives a PT1 filter (PR #14922). PR #15361 changed it to 0.1 Hz per step with a default of 30 (3 Hz), and PR #15485 narrowed the range to 10-50 and moved the filtering onto the position controller's P/A/F terms.
downgrade:ap-position-cutoff-unit-and-fi.note: Position hold's cutoff uses a different unit, range and filter in 2025.12.5, so your value can't be translated and the board's default is used instead. If you had tuned it, tune it again. In 2025.12.5 the value is in 0.01 Hz steps, from 10 to 250.

downgrade:baro-hardware-new-sensors-rese.detail: PR #15009 added the BMP580 and BMP581 options and PR #15302 added SPA06_003. None of them exist in 2025.12.5.
downgrade:baro-hardware-new-sensors-rese.note: 2025.12.5 has no option for the barometer you selected, so the board's default barometer setting is used instead. After flashing, check that a barometer is detected before relying on altitude features.

downgrade:cpu-overclock-reset.detail: PR #14999 moved the overclock frequency options into per-platform defines and changed how the stored value maps to a frequency, so the same option may not mean the same speed in both versions.
downgrade:cpu-overclock-reset.note: The overclock options were reorganised between these versions, so your setting isn't carried over and the board runs at its default speed. If you want to overclock, run `get cpu_overclock` in the CLI to see the options your board offers, then set one again, e.g. `set cpu_overclock = 216MHZ`.

downgrade:custom-mag-alignment-direction.detail: PR #14849 made the newer firmware negate the roll, pitch and yaw custom mag alignment angles before building the rotation, while 2025.12.5 uses the stored values as they are. Flipping the sign keeps the orientation the same.
downgrade:custom-mag-alignment-direction.note: Your custom compass alignment angles were converted for you. 2025.12.5 turns these angles the opposite way, so the converter flipped their signs to keep the same physical mounting. You don't need to do anything, but it's worth checking that the compass heading looks right after flashing.

downgrade:debug-mode-autopilot-values-re.detail: PR #14922 added the AUTOPILOT_PID debug mode and PR #15150 added AUTOPILOT_STOP. Neither exists in 2025.12.5.
downgrade:debug-mode-autopilot-values-re.note: The debug mode you chose doesn't exist in 2025.12.5, so the board's default is used instead. This only changes what debug data goes into blackbox logs, not how the quad flies. Pick another debug mode if you need one.

downgrade:displayport-fbosd-reset.detail: PR #14882 added FBOSD as a new last entry in the OSD displayport device list, with an RP2350 implementation. Earlier versions don't have this entry.
downgrade:displayport-fbosd-reset.note: The framebuffer OSD device (FBOSD) doesn't exist in 2025.12.5 and has no equivalent there, so your board's own default OSD device is used. If you need a specific one, choose from NONE, AUTO, MAX7456, MSP or FRSKYOSD, e.g. `set osd_displayport_device = AUTO`.

downgrade:dronecan-support-not-in-2025-1.detail: PR #15137 added the DroneCAN protocol stack, and PRs #15143 and #15350 added the GNSS and ESC support built on it. None of that exists in 2025.12.5.
downgrade:dronecan-support-not-in-2025-1.note: DroneCAN doesn't exist in 2025.12.5. Any DroneCAN device you use on 2026.6.1 will not work after the downgrade, so plan another way to connect it.

downgrade:feature-rx-msp-removed.detail: PR #14861 added the missing RX_MSP feature name to the CLI in 2026.6.1. Older versions can't set it from CLI text.
downgrade:feature-rx-msp-removed.note: 2025.12.5 has the MSP receiver feature, but its CLI has no name for it, so the board keeps its default for this feature. If you use an MSP receiver, turn it on in the Betaflight Configurator App after loading.

downgrade:feature-rx-udp-removed.detail: PR #15164 added RX_UDP as a selectable feature for the receiver provider on SITL builds. Older firmware doesn't have this feature.
downgrade:feature-rx-udp-removed.note: This feature selects the UDP receiver input used by SITL (simulator) builds, and 2025.12.5 has no way to turn it on. It doesn't affect real flight controllers. If you run a simulator, you'll need to set up its receiver input another way on 2025.12.5.

downgrade:gps-provider-dronecan-reset.detail: PR #15143 added DRONECAN as a GPS provider after 2025.12.5. The older version only has NMEA, UBLOX, MSP and VIRTUAL.
downgrade:gps-provider-dronecan-reset.note: 2025.12.5 cannot read a GPS over DroneCAN, so your board's default GPS provider applies. If you fly with a serial GPS module, set the provider it uses, e.g. `set gps_provider = UBLOX` (NMEA, MSP and VIRTUAL are also available).

downgrade:gps-rescue-distance-minimum-ra.detail: PR #15382 lowered the minimum of these GPS Rescue distance settings from 10 to 5 m. Older firmware still needs at least 10.
downgrade:gps-rescue-distance-minimum-ra.note: 2025.12.5 doesn't accept GPS Rescue distances below 10 m, so values of 5 to 9 were raised to 10. Other values carry over unchanged. Check that 10 m still works for where you fly.

downgrade:mag-hardware-new-sensors-reset.detail: PR #14924 added MMC560X, PR #15174 added QMC5883P and PR #15430 added DRONECAN to the magnetometer table after 2025.12.5. The older version has no matching drivers for them.
downgrade:mag-hardware-new-sensors-reset.note: Your selected magnetometer driver is not in 2025.12.5, so your board's default magnetometer setting applies. To let the firmware look for a supported sensor, use `set mag_hardware = AUTO`. If your compass isn't on the supported list, it won't work in this version.

downgrade:motor-protocol-dronecan-reset.detail: PR #15350 added DRONECAN as a motor output protocol after 2025.12.5. The older version only has the PWM, OneShot, Multishot, Brushed, DShot and ProShot protocols, plus DISABLED.
downgrade:motor-protocol-dronecan-reset.note: 2025.12.5 cannot drive ESCs over DroneCAN, so your board's default motor protocol applies. Before you arm, check that your ESCs work with a supported protocol and set it, e.g. `set motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT600`.

downgrade:optical-flow-poshold-settings-.detail: PR #14922 added optical flow position and altitude hold, including the position source selector and the optical flow range and quality limits. 2025.12.5 does not have these.
downgrade:optical-flow-poshold-settings-.note: Optical flow position hold doesn't exist in 2025.12.5.

downgrade:opticalflow-upt1-reset.detail: PR #14922 added UPT1 optical flow support after 2025.12.5. The older version only has NONE and MT.
downgrade:opticalflow-upt1-reset.note: 2025.12.5 does not support the UPT1 optical flow sensor, so optical flow is set to NONE and won't be used. The only sensor this version supports is MT (`set opticalflow_hardware = MT`).

downgrade:pinio-box-autopilot-ids-disabl.detail: The newer firmware added box IDs 56 (AUTOPILOT) and 57 (WP CAPTURE) at the end of the list, and existing IDs kept their meaning. Only those two IDs have no equivalent in 2025.12.5.
downgrade:pinio-box-autopilot-ids-disabl.note: 2025.12.5 has no autonomous navigation, so the AUTOPILOT (56) and WP CAPTURE (57) modes don't exist there. Any PINIO output linked to one of them is now unassigned (255). All your other PINIO assignments carry over unchanged.

downgrade:position-controller-gains-retu.detail: PR #15485 rebuilt position control in 2026.6.1 around a velocity loop with a new position estimator and different gain scaling. PR #15361 redefined the I term and made the A gain also set how much the estimator trusts the accelerometer.
downgrade:position-controller-gains-retu.note: The position hold gains mean different things in 2025.12.5 than in 2026.6.1, so your tuned values would not fly the same. They go back to 2025.12.5's defaults. Test position hold carefully and re-tune if needed, e.g. `set ap_position_p = <value>`.

downgrade:qmc5883l-renamed-to-qmc5883.detail: PR #15174 renamed the QMC5883 entry to QMC5883L without changing its stored value, and added a separate QMC5883P entry. Going back to 2025.12.5 just restores the old name.
downgrade:qmc5883l-renamed-to-qmc5883.note: This is the same compass chip under its older name. 2025.12.5 calls it QMC5883, so the converter wrote that name in and your compass selection still works the same way.

downgrade:rangefinder-new-sensors-reset.detail: UPT1 was added in PR #14922, and the NOOPLOOP_* sensors are also in the 2026.6.1 list but not in 2025.12.5. All other rangefinder values carry over unchanged.
downgrade:rangefinder-new-sensors-reset.note: 2025.12.5 has no driver for this rangefinder, so it is set to NONE and the rangefinder is off. If you fit a sensor that 2025.12.5 supports, choose it again, e.g. `set rangefinder_hardware = MTF01`.

downgrade:resource-index-numbering-from-.detail: PR #15338 introduced zero-based resource numbering for these targets in 2026.6.1. The stored pin assignments are the same in both versions, only the number shown in the CLI differs.
downgrade:resource-index-numbering-from-.note: On RP2350A and RP2350B boards, 2025.12.5 numbers serial, inverter, SPI, I2C and PIO UART resources from 1, while 2026.6.1 numbers them from 0. The index was raised by one, so each pin stays on the same peripheral. Nothing changes on other boards.

downgrade:resource-index-numbering-not-e.detail: PR #15338 changed how some targets number resource indexes in the CLI, and 2026.6.1 adds CAN_TX/RX/SILENT resources that 2025.12.5 has no equivalent for.
downgrade:resource-index-numbering-not-e.note: This pin assignment can't be written in 2025.12.5 (for example, the CAN pins don't exist there), so the pin keeps the board's default. After loading, check your pin assignments with `resource` and set any pins you still need.

downgrade:scheduler-debug-task-reset.detail: The task count grew from 40 to 42 between these versions, so the allowed range is smaller in 2025.12.5, and task numbers may point to different tasks.
downgrade:scheduler-debug-task-reset.note: This is a debug-only setting that picks which task's timing shows in debug output. It doesn't affect flight and goes back to 0. If you need it, set it again with `set scheduler_debug_task = <number>` (0 to 40), and check that the number points to the task you want.

downgrade:thrust-linear-curve-changed.detail: PR #15226 replaced the cubic thrust curve and its throttle compensation with a Taylor-expanded shape. The name, range 0..150 and scale stayed the same, so no exact conversion exists between versions.
downgrade:thrust-linear-curve-changed.note: The thrust linearization curve is different in 2025.12.5, so the same number gives a different motor response. The setting goes back to 0 (off). If you use it, test and re-tune in each PID profile, then set your value with `set thrust_linear = ` and a number from 0 to 150.

downgrade:transponder-provider-settings-.detail: PR #15126 added these settings to the CLI in 2026.6.1. 2025.12.5 has no such settings.
downgrade:transponder-provider-settings-.note: The transponder provider and transponder data can't be set from the CLI in 2025.12.5. If you use a transponder, check its setup in 2025.12.5 after flashing.

downgrade:waypoint-command-not-in-target.detail: The waypoint CLI command, flight-plan storage and AUTOPILOT mode were added in 2026.6.1 by PR #15030 and extended by later PRs such as #15416 and #15443.
downgrade:waypoint-command-not-in-target.note: 2025.12.5 has no autopilot waypoint missions, so a stored mission can't be carried over. Keep a copy of your 2026.6.1 configuration if you want to restore the mission after upgrading again.

upgrade:altitude-controller-gains-reset.detail: PR #14922 rebuilt the altitude controller as a cascade, and PR #15299 replaced it with a simpler PID. PR #15303 retuned the gains, fixed the feedforward scaling and raised the defaults from 15 to 30.
upgrade:altitude-controller-gains-reset.note: The altitude hold controller was reworked, so your old altitude gains may not behave the same way. They are set to the new default of 30. Test altitude hold carefully at a safe height, then retune from there if needed.

upgrade:cpu-overclock-reset.detail: PR #14999 moved the overclock frequency options from settings.c into per-platform defines and changed how the stored setting maps to a CPU frequency.
upgrade:cpu-overclock-reset.note: The overclock options are now defined separately for each processor family, so your old choice may not mean the same speed in 2026.6.1. Your board's default speed is used instead, which is safe; at worst the processor runs slower. If you want to overclock again, use `set cpu_overclock = <value>` with a value your board accepts.

upgrade:custom-mag-alignment-direction-r.detail: PR #14849 made the firmware negate the custom magnetometer roll, pitch and yaw before building the rotation, where earlier versions used the raw values.
upgrade:custom-mag-alignment-direction-r.note: 2026.6.1 turns the custom compass alignment angles the opposite way. The values were negated, so the same physical mounting gives the same result. No action is needed, though a quick heading check after flashing doesn't hurt.

upgrade:debug-mode-autopilot-position-re.detail: PR #15240 removed the AUTOPILOT_POSITION debug mode name. Other autopilot debug modes were added in PR #14922 and PR #15150.
upgrade:debug-mode-autopilot-position-re.note: The AUTOPILOT_POSITION debug mode no longer exists, so your board's default debug mode is used. This only changes what debug data is recorded, not how the quad flies. If you need debug data, choose another mode with `set debug_mode = <mode>`.

upgrade:gps-rescue-rework-settings-remov.detail: PR #15382 reworked GPS rescue, and these settings are no longer part of it. PR #15030 added new ap_* autopilot settings in the same release.
upgrade:gps-rescue-rework-settings-remov.note: GPS Rescue was reworked in 2026.6.1 and these settings are no longer part of it. Check the GPS rescue behaviour in the new version with a safe test before relying on it.

upgrade:mag-hardware-qmc5883-renamed.detail: PR #15174 renamed QMC5883 to QMC5883L, keeping the same stored value, and added a separate QMC5883P option.
upgrade:mag-hardware-qmc5883-renamed.note: The QMC5883 compass option is now called QMC5883L in 2026.6.1. It is the same chip and the same setting, so your compass selection carries over unchanged.

upgrade:pos-hold-without-mag-removed.detail: PR #15240 removed the setting. Heading validity is now decided by whether GPS contributes to the position estimate.
upgrade:pos-hold-without-mag-removed.note: There is no replacement setting, so there is nothing to set again. Position hold now decides on its own whether the heading is known.

upgrade:position-controller-gains-reset.detail: PR #15485 moved position control to a velocity-loop controller with a new position estimator and different gain scaling, also used by GPS rescue (PR #15382). PR #15361 redefined the I and A terms; A now also sets how much the estimator trusts the accelerometer.
upgrade:position-controller-gains-reset.note: The position hold and GPS rescue position controller was rebuilt in 2026.6.1, so tuned position gains no longer mean the same thing and have been set back to the new default of 30. Fly with the defaults first, then re-tune if needed, e.g. `set ap_position_p = <value>`.

upgrade:position-cutoff-unit-and-filter-.detail: PR #15361 changed the scaling from 0.01 Hz to 0.1 Hz per step and the default from 80 (0.8 Hz) to 30 (3 Hz). PR #15485 narrowed the range to 10-50 (1-5 Hz) and moved the filtering onto the P/A/F terms.
upgrade:position-cutoff-unit-and-filter-.note: The position controller's cutoff now uses a different unit (0.1 Hz steps instead of 0.01 Hz), a narrower range (10-50) and a different filter, so your old value has no direct equivalent. The 2026.6.1 default of 30 (3 Hz) is used. If you had tuned it, start from the default and retune in flight; the value is the cutoff in Hz times ten, e.g. `set ap_position_cutoff = 30` for 3 Hz.

upgrade:resource-index-numbering-from-ze.detail: PR #15338 changed how resource indexes are shown and entered on targets that number bus peripherals from zero. The stored pin assignments themselves did not change, only the number shown in the CLI.
upgrade:resource-index-numbering-from-ze.note: On RP2350A and RP2350B boards, 2026.6.1 numbers serial, inverter, SPI, I2C and PIO UART resources from 0 instead of 1. The index was lowered by one, so each pin stays on the same peripheral. Nothing changes on other boards, and nothing needs to be done.

upgrade:scheduler-debug-task-reset.detail: The task count grew from 40 to 42, which raised the setting's maximum. PR #14958 kept the default at 0.
upgrade:scheduler-debug-task-reset.note: Two scheduler tasks were added in 2026.6.1, so a task number from your old config may now point to a different task. The default of 0 is used. This only affects debug output, not flight; if you were profiling a task, find its new number and set it with `set scheduler_debug_task = <number>`.

upgrade:thrust-linear-curve-changed.detail: PR #15226 replaced the cubic thrust-linearization curve and its throttle compensation with a curve that is closer to thrust-stand data. The name, the 0..150 range and the /100 scale did not change, so there is no exact conversion for non-zero values.
upgrade:thrust-linear-curve-changed.note: Thrust linearization now uses a different curve, so the same number gives a different motor response. It is off (0) for now. If you used it, re-tune and set your new value in each PID profile with `set thrust_linear = <value>` (0 to 150).

set:dronecan_node_id|downgrade|*.comment: The DroneCAN node ID has no use in 2025.12.5 because DroneCAN is not supported

set:gps_provider|downgrade|0.comment: DroneCAN GPS isn't supported in 2025.12.5; board default applies. Set NMEA, UBLOX, MSP or VIRTUAL

set:gps_rescue_descent_dist|downgrade|*.comment: raised to 10 m if it was lower, because 2025.12.5 doesn't accept anything below 10

set:gps_rescue_disarm_threshold|downgrad.comment: GPS rescue setting that exists again in 2025.12.5; it starts at its board default, so check it.

set:gps_rescue_disarm_threshold|upgrade|.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_imu_yaw_gain|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_max_angle|downgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue max angle exists again in 2025.12.5; it starts at its board default, so check it.

set:gps_rescue_max_angle|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_min_start_dist|downgrade|.comment: raised to 10 m if it was lower, because 2025.12.5 doesn't accept anything below 10

set:gps_rescue_pitch_cutoff|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_roll_mix|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_use_mag|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old setting has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_velocity_d|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old tuning value has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_velocity_i|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old tuning value has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:gps_rescue_velocity_p|upgrade|*.comment: GPS rescue was reworked; this old tuning value has no direct equivalent, so re-check rescue behaviour

set:mag_align_pitch|downgrade|*.comment: sign flipped because 2025.12.5 turns custom compass alignment the other way; mounting stays the same

set:mag_align_pitch|upgrade|*.comment: custom compass rotation direction was reversed, so the value was negated to keep the same mounting

set:mag_align_roll|downgrade|*.comment: sign flipped because 2025.12.5 turns custom compass alignment the other way; mounting stays the same

set:mag_align_roll|upgrade|*.comment: custom compass rotation direction was reversed, so the value was negated to keep the same mounting

set:mag_align_yaw|downgrade|*.comment: sign flipped because 2025.12.5 turns custom compass alignment the other way; mounting stays the same

set:mag_align_yaw|upgrade|*.comment: custom compass rotation direction was reversed, so the value was negated to keep the same mounting

set:mag_hardware|downgrade|*.comment: QMC5883L is named QMC5883 in 2025.12.5; it's the same compass, so the converter swapped in the old name

set:mag_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: this compass driver isn't in 2025.12.5; board default applies. Try `set mag_hardware = AUTO`

set:mag_hardware|upgrade|*.comment: QMC5883 is now named QMC5883L; same chip, so the selection carries over

set:motor_pwm_protocol|downgrade|0.comment: DroneCAN ESC output isn't in 2025.12.5; board default applies. Set a protocol your ESCs support

set:opticalflow_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: UPT1 sensor isn't supported in 2025.12.5; optical flow is set to NONE (only MT is available)

set:osd_displayport_device|downgrade|0.comment: FBOSD doesn't exist in 2025.12.5; your board's default OSD device applies

set:pinio_box|downgrade|*.comment: AUTOPILOT (56) and WP CAPTURE (57) don't exist in 2025.12.5 and are now 255; other values carry over

set:pos_hold_without_mag|upgrade|*.comment: heading validity for position hold is now derived from whether GPS contributes; no setting needed

set:poshold_opticalflow_max_range|downgr.comment: optical flow position hold is new in 2026.6.1, so its range limit has no equivalent in 2025.12.5

set:poshold_opticalflow_quality_min|down.comment: optical flow position hold is new in 2026.6.1, so its quality threshold has no equivalent in 2025.12.5

set:poshold_position_source|downgrade|*.comment: the position source selector came with optical flow position hold, which 2025.12.5 doesn't have

set:rangefinder_hardware|downgrade|0.comment: 2025.12.5 has no driver for this sensor, so the rangefinder is set to NONE (off)

set:scheduler_debug_task|downgrade|*.comment: debug-only setting reset to 0; task numbers may differ in 2025.12.5, so check before setting it again

set:scheduler_debug_task|upgrade|*.comment: two tasks were added, so task numbers may have shifted; the default of 0 is used (debug output only)

set:thrust_linear|downgrade|*.comment: the thrust curve differs in 2025.12.5, so the same value acts differently; reset to 0, re-tune if you use it

set:thrust_linear|upgrade|*.comment: the thrust curve changed, so the old value no longer gives the same response; re-tune it

set:transponder_data|downgrade|*.comment: Transponder data can't be set from the CLI in 2025.12.5, so check your transponder after flashing

set:transponder_data|upgrade|*.comment: Transponder ID data can now be set from the CLI; it stays at the default until you set it.

set:transponder_provider|downgrade|*.comment: Transponder provider can't be set from the CLI in 2025.12.5, so check your transponder after flashing

set:transponder_provider|upgrade|*.comment: Transponder type (NONE, ILAP, ARCITIMER, ERLT) is now a CLI setting; it defaults to ILAP.

set:trust_mag|upgrade|*.comment: New magnetometer trust option, OFF by default.
